title: The ghoul of Karaikkal
word: in their own words where they exist
hookLine: a poet signs her hymns as a ghoul of the cremation ground, where Shiva dances: Karaikkal Ammaiyar, and why Shaivas wear sacred ash
carry: sacred ash: all burns, shiva remains
tomorrow: a sealed room, a king, and palm leaves eaten by ants.

cards: At the end of a hymn, the poet signs her name. This poet doesn't sign as a saint, or a lady, or a devotee. She signs as a pey, a ghoul, the kind of gaunt spirit said to haunt the burning grounds.
The pey of Karaikkal. Earlier on this path we met her at her own door, giving away a mango. Today, the name she gave herself.

teach.h: PUNITAVATI ASKS FOR A NEW BODY
teach.b: Her story is in the Periya Puranam, the book of the lives of the Shaiva saints. Her name was Punitavati, a merchant's wife in Karaikkal. After the mango, her husband grew afraid of her and left.
So she asked Shiva to take away the beauty she had kept for him, and give her the body of a pey instead, bones and sinew, fit only for praising him.
The story says she climbed Shiva's mountain upside down, so her feet wouldn't touch its holy ground, and that Shiva, seeing her, called her Mother.

teach.h: SHE SIGNS AS THE PEY OF KARAIKKAL
teach.b: So she's known as Karaikkal Ammaiyar, the mother of Karaikkal. Now her own words, in paraphrase.
Her hymns picture Shiva dancing at night in the cremation ground, among flames, ash and owls, with ghouls dancing around him. Among them is the singer herself, signing as the pey of Karaikkal.
She didn't hide the bones; she signed with them. In Shaiva tradition Shiva is the Lord of the burning ground, the one who is there when everything else has gone to ash.

Many Shaiva teachers give the same meaning to vibhuti, the sacred ash devotees wear in three lines on the forehead: everything ends in ash, and Shiva remains. Shiva himself is pictured smeared in ash.
She took that to its edge, and stopped dressing up for anyone. And today? When looks, titles and what people call you start to feel like everything, the ash on a Shaiva forehead says: those burn.
What you give to Shiva remains. Her hymns are kept in the Tirumurai, the sacred Shaiva collection, and with her, this season of women closes.

how: Tamil Shaivas honor Karaikkal Ammaiyar among the Nayanars; her hymns are sung as part of the Tirumurai, her image is found in Shiva temples near the dancing Shiva, and devotees wear vibhuti, sacred ash, on the forehead.

games.q: what does “in their own words where they exist” mean?
o: only the stories later writers told about saints
the words of saints, rewritten in modern Tamil
women's voices, where their own words have come down

games.q: two names for one poet — tap the pairs.
p: her name before she was a saint
the name the story says Shiva gave her
the name she signs in her hymns
where her Shiva dances at night

s: in her hymns, Karaikkal Ammaiyar signs herself as a saint and a lady
she signs as the pey of Karaikkal, a ghoul of the burning ground.
in the story, she climbs Shiva's mountain upside down
so her feet won't touch its holy ground.
Shaivas often wear sacred ash in three lines across the forehead
vibhuti, which many teachers read as: all burns, Shiva remains.

games.q: at Shivaratri, a cousin asks why Shiva, of all gods, dances in a cremation ground. by Karaikkal Ammaiyar's hymns, what fits?
o: he's the Lord who remains when everything turns to ash, so his devotee needn't fear the end.
it's a punishment; he was banished there.
it's just a scary story to keep kids home at night.
games.why: she sings Shiva dancing among the fires, and herself among his ghouls. for Shaivas he is the one who remains when all else is ash.

practice: If your family keeps vibhuti, take a small pinch; if not, just touch your thumb to your forehead. Many Shaivas draw the ash in three lines, some saying namah shivaya as they do. Think, gently: this body will end in ash.

Not as a scare; as a relief. Let the names people call you, the roles, the looks, settle like ash, one at a time. If you pray, offer what's left to Shiva; if you don't, sit with what remains when those are gone.

wordCard.voice: In their own words, where they exist: Karaikkal Ammaiyar, called Mother in the story, who signed her hymns as the pey of Karaikkal. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: sacred ash, all burns, Shiva remains. Mother in the story, pey in her own hand. A season closes here.
